description: Learners should be able to use common techniques to retrieve data from multiple data sources: SQL, NoSQL databases, APIs, Cloud, including Retrieving, Cleaning data.
Learners should be able to describe and use common feature selection and feature engineering techniques, including Exploratory Data Analysis, Feature Engineering, Variable.

Learners should be able to use a variety of techniques for detecting and dealing with outliers, including Inferential Statistics, Hypothesis Testing, Estimation, Inference, Hypothesis Testing (Homework).
Learners should be able to describe and use supervised models, including Introduction to Supervised Machine Learning, Linear Regression.

Learners should be able to use a variety of error metrics to compare and select a supervised model that best suits your data, including Logistic Regression: Introduction to Classification, Error Metrics, Error Metrics, Model Interpretability (Homework).
Learners should be able to use oversampling and undersampling as techniques to handle unbalanced classes in a data, including Modeling Unbalanced Classes, Practice Lab: Modeling Imbalanced Classes.
Learners should be able to explain the kinds of problems suitable for Unsupervised Learning approaches, including Introduction to Unsupervised Learning, K Means.

Explain the curse of dimensionality, and how it makes clustering difficult with many features, including K Means Clustering, Selecting a clustering algorithm, Distance Metrics of Clustering Algorithms, Common clustering algorithms, Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering, Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering Lab, Compare clustering, Dimensionality Reduction.

Learners should be able to describe and use common clustering and dimensionality-reduction algorithms, including Selecting a clustering algorithm, Distance Metrics of Clustering Algorithms, Common clustering algorithms, Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering, Hierarchical Agglomerative Clustering Lab, Compare clustering algorithms, Clustering Demo.

Implement a mini capstone ML project includes steps: data collection, data wrangling, exploratory data analysis, model development, model evaluation, and reporting, including Guiding mini Capstone, Review the mini Capstone, Review mini Capstone.
